name: Dusky plum
lede: Dusky plum is a dark, muted reddish purple, the 2010 xkcd survey's shaded take on the fruit color [[plum]].

sections.title: A fruit, dimmed
sections.body:
Our only recorded source for this name is the 2010 xkcd crowd color survey, with nothing earlier on file [1]. In the ISCC-NBS 1955 system it falls nearest the block the dictionary calls "dark reddish purple", 7.8 units off, one of the looser matches in our library [2]. In Munsell terms it reads about 1.8RP 3.6/4.7, a dark, moderately saturated red-purple [2].

The word "dusky" lowers the color's lightness and takes some of the shine off the ripe plum it is named for, pushing it toward grey [2]. The nearest named colors on file are [[dull-dark-purple]], [[raisin-purple]] and [[old-lilac]], at 2.6, 4.4 and 4.7 ΔE [2]. Who first wrote the pairing down is undocumented in the sources we hold [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in only 12 of 23,781 paintings, about one in two thousand, as photographed; this is one of the rarer matches among our color names [3]. The earliest dated match is Jacopo Bassano's *Adoration of the Magi*, from 1568, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. Of its matches, about a third sit as the darkest shadow area in their painting, more often than most colors in our archive play that role [3]. Too few paintings share it to name a leading painter or decade with confidence [3]. These counts are a computed color match on photographs of aged, varnished paintings, not a pigment test [3].

questions.q: What does the word "dusky" do to the fruit color plum here?
choices: Nothing; the two names are identical in color
